title: Olive Finds the Trail
checkpoint: Year 1 Spring 1, week 4 — School readiness — Phase 5: new ways to say and spell ch, ow, ie
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — new graphemes eigh, ei, ey.

pages.text: Olive spots wet marks on the path.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl perched on a low branch at dusk, looking down at a row of small wet marks on a garden path.

pages.text: The marks are not from Olive.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl lifting one foot, comparing the shape of her own foot to the wet marks on the path below.

pages.text: Olive wants to see where they go.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl tilting her head, following the line of wet marks with her eyes along the path.

pages.text: Olive swoops down low to look.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl swooping low over the garden path, wings spread, eyes fixed on the trail of marks.

pages.text: The marks go past the big oak tree.
pages.illustration: The trail of wet marks continuing along the path, passing the thick trunk of a big oak tree.

pages.text: The marks go past the old barn.
pages.illustration: The trail of wet marks leading past the open doorway of an old wooden barn.

pages.text: The marks stop at the pond.
pages.illustration: The row of wet marks ending at the grassy edge of a round garden pond.

pages.text: Ned pops up out of the pond!
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling popping up out of the pond with a splash, water dripping from his yellow-brown feathers.

pages.text: The wet feet of Ned make the marks.
pages.illustration: A close view of Ned the duckling standing on the bank, his wet orange feet matching the marks on the path.

pages.text: Olive and Ned grin at the wet trail.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl and Ned the duckling standing together by the pond, both looking at the trail of wet marks and grinning.
